claim: 17: bit7 selects global table; bit6 selects K (1) versus c (0); low six bits count captures. Global slots are absolute; local slots add constitution base with 16-bit arithmetic.
limits: Non-global K is outside the selected future implementation; absence in corpus is not native rejection.

claim: Creation saves pFunctions[funOffset].f and independently retains current thisObject when live, even for a global target. Global-created values can have a null owner.
limits: No general validation of arbitrary malformed table entries is proven; owner reference is not the callee execution context.

claim: 05 rejects a saved deleted owner before K/c dispatch, including global targets. vm_copyValue can clean the source and produce Undefined; the owner-null case is not invalidated by this test.
limits: Rust logical deletion still differs from native ref/execRef and deferred deletion. Raw call and prior ordinary copy must remain distinct.

claim: c dispatch passes saved pFun, stored funOffset and isGlobal to vm_callInUserFunBody. A Global callee clears thisObject, uses current vm_pGlobalProgram constitution and saved pFun code segment.
limits: The combination of saved code and current global constitution does not prove arbitrary hot replacement is coherent.

claim: K dispatch reads a signed slot at saved descriptor+0x1a, then vm_callInEfun fetches current global pFunctions[slot] and invokes its native entry. It does not directly invoke the saved pointer as a callback.
limits: Native efun descriptors are assumed alive by this path; no descriptor unload lifetime guarantee is established.

claim: Efun activation copies 40 bytes of caller context, then replaces bp, argNum, flags and f. Its thisObject/code context is inherited from the invocation caller, not from the saved function owner.
limits: ctrlFlags, scheduler, reentry and next-action hooks remain outside a synchronous Rust subset.

claim: Captured arguments precede new arguments for both K and c. Unique function heads move captures; shared heads copy through vm_pushValue/vm_copyValue. Scalar captures avoid the selected non-scalar normalization difference.
limits: Not proof that arbitrary Object/Array/Mapping/Function captures are equivalent under Rc cloning.

claim: Efun return processing uses its own exact/Mixed/Void result contract; user-body entry is a different path. Final function-head cleanup releases captures and saved owner.
limits: Not a proof of all efun argument conventions or general exception recovery.

claim: Global finalization installs pFun into the compiling program table and can retain hidden function definitions. This establishes table update sites, not complete lifetime safety for arbitrary saved entries after recompilation.
limits: Compiler, hidden functions, unload and cross-generation constitution compatibility remain unresolved.

claim: First implementation: scalar-capturing Global user targets snapshot ProgramId/function at creation; new calls require that same Global program still be bound. Entered frames keep their saved code if binding later changes.
limits: Reject clear/rebind before entry with InvalidState rather than inventing native hot-reload semantics; direct 07 continues resolving the current binding.

claim: Second implementation: global K targets require an explicitly registered synchronous host slot at creation, save canonical slot identity, and resolve current callback/signature at each invocation. No real efun implementation is added.
limits: Synthetic registry replacement is a bounded Rust policy analogous to late table lookup, not native registration/unload equivalence.

claim: Represent optional creator owner separately from Object/Global/Host target; make public owner/program access optional and expose a typed target descriptor. Preserve origin-token identity and pointer equality.
limits: This requires a documented source-breaking accessor migration in the future implementation; this evidence-only stage changes no public API.

claim: General non-scalar captures, cyclic graph reclamation, all early copy cleanup sites and owner deferred deletion are not closed.
limits: G06/G07/G14 remain dependencies; all non-scalar captures stay rejected.

claim: String/OS targets, non-global K, hidden/inherited targets, lifecycle/default-expression creation, general catch/hook and dynamic service execution are not part of the two implementation batches.
limits: No static count or name match proves runtime reachability or service compatibility.
